name: Randall: PM25 Dataset for the United States
description: The Washington University in St. Louis Atmospheric Composition Analysis Group (ACAG) Surface PM2.5 dataset provides satellite-derived estimates of ground-level fine particulate matter concentrations. Global and regional PM2.5 concentrations are estimated using information from satellite-, simulation-, and monitor-based sources. Aerosol optical depth from multiple satellite instruments (MODIS/Terra, MODIS/Aqua, MISR/Terra, SeaWiFS/SeaStar, VIIRS/SNPP, and VIIRS/NOAA20) and their respective retrievals (Dark Target, Deep Blue, MAIAC) is combined with the GEOS-Chem chemical transport model based upon their relative uncertainties as determined using ground-based sun photometer (AERONET) observations. This dataset includes two algorithm versions: V5GL (traditional global algorithm using Geographically Weighted Regression) and V6GL (state-of-the-science algorithm using a residual Convolutional Neural Network). Estimates are available monthly and yearly at ZCTA and county levels for the United States.

name: PM25 Randall V5GL
description: PM25 estimates from the V5.GL.05.02 algorithm, representing the traditional global algorithm for satellite-derived PM2.5 estimates. This version estimates annual and monthly ground-level fine particulate matter for 1998-2023 by combining Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) retrievals (Dark Target, Deep Blue, and MAIAC) from multiple satellite-based NASA instruments (MODIS/Terra, MODIS/Aqua, MISR/Terra, SeaWiFS/SeaStar, VIIRS/SNPP, and VIIRS/NOAA20) with the GEOS-Chem chemical transport model, and subsequently calibrating to global ground-based observations using Geographically Weighted Regression (GWR). This version updates the ground-based observations used to calibrate the geophysical PM2.5 estimates for the entire time series and includes retrievals from the SNPP/NOAA VIIRS instruments.

name: PM25 Randall V6GL
description: PM25 estimates from the V6.GL.02.04 algorithm, representing the most state-of-the-science global algorithm for satellite-derived PM2.5 estimates. This version estimates annual and monthly ground-level fine particulate matter for 1998-2023 by combining Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) retrievals (Dark Target, Deep Blue, MAIAC) from numerous satellite-based NASA instruments (MODIS/Terra, MODIS/Aqua, MISR/Terra, SeaWiFS/SeaStar, VIIRS/SNPP, and VIIRS/NOAA20) with the GEOS-Chem chemical transport model, and subsequently calibrating to global ground-based observations using a residual Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). V6.GL.02.04 includes updated ground-based observations for the entire time series, extends temporal coverage through 2023, includes retrievals from the SNPP VIIRS instrument, and addresses previous limitations with abnormally low values using a modified padding strategy and stronger geophysical constraints.
